title: Customer Service & Sales Fundamentals
description: The daily work of serving and selling at Greens, at the counter and on the phone: who our customers are, the service standard, the nine parts of a sales call, recommending a size, the 22-item call score sheet, walk-ins and tours, move-ins done right, web leads, honest answers to objections, existing tenants and rate changes, collections with respect, difficult situations, reviews, twenty practice scenarios and a one-page job aid. Course 5 of the Greens Storage Academy.
overview: Who calls and walks in, what they are going through, and why the first good conversation wins
The Greens service standard and the response times every site works to
The nine parts of a sales call, with sample words, and recommending a size instead of asking for one
The 22-item call score sheet used again in the Hands-On Check
Walk-ins, the tour, a move-in done right, and following up on web leads within minutes
Honest answers to objections, existing tenants, and the "why did my rent go up" call
Collections with respect, difficult situations and reviews
Twenty practice scenarios and a one-page job aid

questions.q: A caller at Escondido says she is clearing out her late father's condo and apologizes for rambling. What do you do first?
options: Quote the 10x10 rate so she has a number to work with
Say you are sorry and ask what furniture there is
Ask her to call back once she knows the size she wants
Tell her about this month's move-in special first
questions.explanation: She needs calm help, not a pitch. Condolence, then a question that moves her forward. Quoting a rate first treats a grieving caller like a price shopper.

questions.q: A caller asks, "How late are you open?" You give the hours. What comes next?
options: Thank her for calling and end the call politely
Ask if she is renting or calling about an account
Read her the full list of unit sizes and prices
Point her to the website for everything else she needs
questions.explanation: Answer the question, then ask why she called. Most staff stop at the hours, and the rental goes to the next site that asks.

questions.q: You are with a customer at the counter and the phone rings. What do you do?
options: Let it ring; the counter customer comes first
Excuse yourself, take a number, call back soon
Answer and finish the whole call, then return
Ask the counter customer to wait outside for a while
questions.explanation: The counter customer comes first, but a missed call is a rental handed away. Take the name and number and call back when you said.

questions.q: A first-time renter asks which size she should get. What is your next step?
options: Ask what size she thinks she needs today
Ask what she is storing, then recommend
Send her the size chart and let her choose
Quote the smallest unit so the price looks good
questions.explanation: Never hand a first-timer a decision she cannot make. Ask what she is storing, then recommend a size and say why.

questions.q: A Valley Center caller is storing a one-bedroom apartment. What do you ask about climate control?
options: Whether any of it minds the heat
Nothing; recommend climate control for everyone
Nothing; climate control is only for businesses
Whether she will pay extra for climate control today
questions.explanation: Ask about heat-sensitive items. Climate control helps wood, electronics, photos and instruments; pushing it for everything is an add-on customers resent.

questions.q: You are quoting a 10x15 on the phone. Which price is complete?
options: Rent only, since fees come up at move-in
Rent, special and its end, admin fee, protection
Rent and the special, without when the special ends
Rent plus your best guess at the first payment amount
questions.explanation: Give the whole price up front; surprise fees are the complaint you are preventing. Run Preview Charges for the first payment, never guess.

questions.q: You scored a call: 22 items, 2 were N/A, and you had 16 Yes. What is the score?
questions.explanation: Items that applied are 22 minus 2, so 20. 16 divided by 20 is 80%, a pass. Dividing by 22 gives 73%, the common mistake.

questions.q: You forgot to ask a caller her move-in date. On the score sheet, that item is a No, not an N/A.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Not asking is a No. N/A is only for an item that could not apply, such as a caller who hung up before a close was possible.

lessons.title: Greens Tenant Protection
lessons.summary: Greens' protection levels and prices, who uses what, and how to offer it at every move-in.

lessons.title: Leads and Reservations in Cubby
lessons.summary: Lead sources and statuses, holding a unit with a reservation, and follow-up tasks.

questions.q: A walk-in at Temecula insists you step inside the far unit with him to measure. What do you do?
options: Step in quickly, measure, and step back out
Stay in the doorway and hand him the tape
Call a coworker over so two of you can go in
Go in first so he follows you, as sales advice says
questions.explanation: Never enter a unit with a prospect or tenant. Stay in the doorway, hand over the tape and call out the numbers.

questions.q: A walk-in liked the unit but says, "I'll think about it." What do you ask?
options: "Would a discount help you decide today?"
"Is it the size, the price or the timing?"
"Can you let me know by tonight, please?"
"Did another site offer you a better deal?"
questions.explanation: Find what is underneath. Then answer it, offer a free hold and a quote sheet, and set a follow-up time.

questions.q: A Valley Center customer reserves a 5x10 online at 10:02 AM, during open hours. When do you call?
options: By 10:07 AM
Before the office closes
First thing tomorrow
Only if she misses move-in
questions.explanation: First live contact within 5 minutes during open hours. Online renters often pick too small; the call is how you catch it.

questions.q: An Abandoned Checkout lead shows up in Cubby at Escondido. What does it usually mean?
options: A spam lead you can safely skip
Someone who started renting and stopped
A tenant who has already moved out of a unit
A finished reservation with nothing left to do
questions.explanation: Abandoned and failed checkouts are warm leads: the person was minutes from renting. Call the same day.

questions.q: A new customer at the counter asks what Greens' protection plan costs. What do you quote?
options: $9 or $20 a month, like many current tenants pay
Whatever price the last move-in was charged
Nothing, because the plan is free for a new tenant
questions.explanation: A new tenant pays today's price. The lower prices are legacy prices on older leases and are never quoted to a new customer.

questions.q: A caller says the place down the road is $20 a month cheaper. What do you do first?
options: Match the price on the spot to win the rental
Acknowledge it and compare total cost
Mention the problems you have heard about that site
Tell her the other price is probably not real
questions.explanation: Acknowledge, then compare total cost: when the special ends, fees, protection, deposit. A match is your manager's decision; never criticize a competitor.

questions.q: At move-in, a tenant asks who can get into her unit. What do you say?
options: "Anyone you list on the account with us"
"Whoever has your gate code and key"
"Only you, no matter who has your code"
"Anyone our manager approves to go in"
questions.explanation: The tenant controls access with the code and the key. Saying it every time makes later access requests simple to answer.

questions.q: A text telling a customer about this month's special is marketing and needs their prior written consent.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A text about a special is marketing under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. A text confirming the customer's own reservation is service, but follows the hours rule.

lessons.title: Greens Waivers, Credits and Refunds
lessons.summary: What a waive, a credit and a refund do, the rules that always apply, and who approves each.

lessons.title: Greens Delinquency Timeline
lessons.summary: The day-by-day collections ladder Cubby runs, and what you do at each step.

lessons.title: Greens Privacy and Records
lessons.summary: Who may hear about an account, police and subpoenas, and what Greens keeps.

questions.q: A caller asks for his wife's balance. She is the tenant; he is not on the account. What do you do?
options: Give the balance, since they are married
Say you can only discuss it with the tenant
Give the balance but not the unit number
Email the balance to him so it is in writing
questions.explanation: Account details go only to the tenant or someone listed and verified. Be kind and firm, and offer to help the tenant right away.

questions.q: A tenant emails a move-out notice. What do you do?
options: Reply by email to confirm the date
Call her, live, within 24 hours
Wait for her to come in to the office
Send the move-out form and nothing else
questions.explanation: A live call within 24 hours: learn why, and help if a save fits. Most move-outs are happy endings; then thank her and ask for a review.

questions.q: A tenant asks you to remove his rate increase. That is above your authority. What do you say?
options: "I'll get it reversed for you today"
"I'll ask my manager; call you by 4:00 PM"
"Nothing can be done about it at all, sorry"
"It won't go up again, I promise you that"
questions.explanation: A concession is your manager's call. Promise only the callback, at a set time, and keep it.

questions.q: A tenant asks how much notice Greens gives before a rate change. You are not sure. What do you do?
options: Tell her 30 days, which is common
Check her agreement or ask your manager
Tell her there is no notice for rate changes
Say the system decides how much notice to give
questions.explanation: The notice comes from the agreement, and your manager has Greens' rules. Never state a notice period you have not read or confirmed.

questions.q: You call about a past-due account and the tenant's roommate answers. What may you say?
options: "Please tell Sam the rent is past due"
Your name, Greens Storage and a number
"It's about a lien on Sam's storage unit"
The balance, so Sam can pay it when home
questions.explanation: Third parties get your first name, Greens Storage and a callback number, never the reason. The same goes for voicemail.

questions.q: A tenant behind on rent can pay half today. What do you tell him before he pays?
options: Half stops the ladder for a month
Half does not stop the ladder
Half resets every date on the ladder
Half is enough to close the account
questions.explanation: Cubby applies money to the oldest charge first, so the lease stays past due. Say so honestly before he decides; payment in full stops the ladder.

questions.q: A coworker says, "Tell him we're selling Monday," but the sale is weeks away. What do you tell the tenant?
options: "We are selling your things on Monday"
The real next step and its date
"Very soon, but I can't say exactly when"
"The system has set the sale for Monday"
questions.explanation: A false date is a misleading statement under the collection laws Greens follows. Give the real step and date, factually.

questions.q: A woman says her ex rents a unit with her furniture in it. You may confirm he rents there as long as you do not open it.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Do not confirm or deny that anyone rents at Greens. Only the tenant controls access; a court order is the path.

questions.q: A Fairfield caller says, "I've got a 30-foot travel trailer and the HOA is on me." What builds trust fastest?
options: Quote the cheapest space you have right now
Ask the length with the tongue and how often it moves
Tell him the gate and office hours for the week
Ask whether the HOA has sent him a written notice yet
questions.explanation: Vehicle customers trust staff who know their world. The overall length with the tongue and how often it moves are the questions that matter.

questions.q: A caller says she only needs storage "for a month or two." How should you treat her?
options: As a quick sale that needs little effort
As the start of a long relationship
As someone not worth a follow-up call later
As a reason to skip the discovery questions
questions.explanation: Customers almost always stay longer than they expect; Greens' average stay is on Greens by the Numbers.

questions.q: Most people who call about storage have already looked at prices or reviews online.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: They shop, then call. The call is near the end of the decision, so it tests you, not only the price.

questions.q: A tenant is upset that his code failed. Put the Greens recovery steps in order.
options: Hear
Own
Solve
Thank
Fix
questions.explanation: Hear before you solve; the common mistake is jumping to Solve and fixing the wrong problem. Fix is the cause, afterward.

questions.q: You promised a 2:00 PM callback, and at 1:45 PM you still have no answer. What do you do?
options: Wait, and call once you have the answer
Call now and give a new time
Send a text saying you are busy today
Skip it; they will call you if they need you
questions.explanation: Call before the promised time and say when you will have it. Customers trust you more for it, not less.

questions.q: A tenant asks you to waive a fee. You are not sure it is within your limit. What do you say?
options: "Yes, consider it done, I'll take it off"
"I'll ask my manager, call you by 4:00 PM"
"We never waive fees here, for anybody"
"Maybe, just check your next bill and see what happens"
questions.explanation: Never promise a waive you are not allowed to give. Above your limit, ask your manager and call back at a set time.

questions.q: You must leave a voicemail for a prospect who asked about a pull-through space. What goes in it?
options: Your number and nothing else, to keep it short
Name, site, the space and price, number, when you'll call
A reminder that prices may go up soon, to create urgency
Every special running this month, so she can compare them
questions.explanation: A message a prospect will return names the space and price they asked about and when you will try again. Then call at that time.

questions.q: A lead that Cubby's voice agent took after hours belongs to the voice agent, so you wait for the customer to call.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A lead taken by someone else is yours the moment you see it. Call, confirm the size fits and confirm the move-in date.

questions.q: Your site is thinking about recording calls. What does California require?
options: Nothing beyond a manager's approval
Everyone's consent, so a notice plays
Only the consent of the employee
Recording on your own phone, not the line
questions.explanation: California needs everyone's consent to record a call. Greens decides whether lines record; never record on your own phone.

questions.q: A caller mentioned her mom's solid-wood dresser. Which line builds value?
options: "We have climate-controlled units available."
"Climate control keeps your mom's dresser safe."
"Our site is clean, safe and very well run."
"We have more units than any other site around here."
questions.explanation: Value is a feature tied to the caller's own words. "We have climate control" is a brochure.

questions.q: A caller likes the unit but is not ready to rent today. Which close fits?
options: "Come by anytime you like this week."
"I can reserve it now at no charge."
"Let me know if you have any questions."
"Give us a call back whenever you're ready."
questions.explanation: The reservation close holds the unit with no charge. "Come by anytime" and "let me know" are not closes.

questions.q: Before you hang up on a new-rental call, which of these should you have? Pick all that apply.
options: Name, phone and email
The move-in date
A set time for the next contact
The caller's employer
questions.explanation: Capture name, phone, email, move date, the unit and price quoted, how they heard about Greens, and a set callback time.

questions.q: A customer asks what his first payment will be. How do you get the number?
options: Estimate it from the monthly rent
Run Preview Charges in Cubby
Use what last week's move-in paid
Tell him you'll know at the counter
questions.explanation: The first payment depends on the move-in date. Preview Charges gives the real number; never guess.

questions.q: A caller wants a 5x10 for a couch, a bed, a table and about 40 boxes. What do you do?
options: Rent her the 5x10, since she asked for it
Say it won't fit and recommend a 10x15
Suggest she rent two 5x10 units side by side
Ask her to measure every piece and call back later
questions.explanation: Recommending the right size is a service. If it will not fit, she finds out on moving day and blames you.

questions.q: You are torn between two sizes for a customer who needs her files every week. What do you do?
options: Pick the smaller one to save her money
Go up a size and say why
Let her pick, so it is her decision
Pick whichever one is cheaper today
questions.explanation: When in doubt, go up a size: a walkway means she is not unstacking everything for one box. Going up is not upselling when you say why.

questions.q: A Temecula contractor mentions a couple of gas cans for his generator. What do you say?
options: "Just keep them near the door"
"We can't store fuel, sorry"
"Fine, as long as they are sealed"
"Only inside a climate-controlled unit"
questions.explanation: Flammables cannot be stored. Screen kindly during discovery, not at move-in.

questions.q: Your mock call scored 92%, but you called the protection plan "insurance." What is the result?
options: Excellent
A pass
Not a pass
A pass with a note
questions.explanation: A wrong price, calling the plan insurance, or an unauthorized promise is never a pass, whatever the percentage.

questions.q: A caller opens with "I rented with you before." How do you mark "Asked whether they had rented before"?
options: No
N/A
Yes
Leave it blank
questions.explanation: N/A is for an item that could not apply. She answered it in her first sentence, so the item does not apply.

questions.q: A couple walks in while you are on the phone. What do you do?
options: Finish the call, then look up and greet them
Smile, raise a finger: "Right with you"
Wave them toward the chairs without a word
Put the caller on hold and start the tour
questions.explanation: Greet within seconds, even on the phone. Then finish quickly and stand up.

questions.q: Where do you ask for the rental on a tour?
options: Back at the office, at the counter
At the unit
At the gate, on the way out
In a text message that evening
questions.explanation: Close at the unit, while they are picturing their things inside.

questions.q: You are alone at Valley Center, it is getting dark, and a prospect wants to see a unit at the back. What do you do?
options: Go quickly, before it gets fully dark
Offer a video now, a tour tomorrow
Give him a code to look on his own
Tell him you are alone, so he understands
questions.explanation: No tours after dark alone, and never say you are alone. A video of the exact unit is a fine substitute.

questions.q: A Fairfield walk-in is not ready to rent. What should he leave with? Pick all that apply.
options: A written quote sheet
A free hold on the space
A set follow-up time
A gate code to look around
questions.explanation: Quote sheet, a free hold, his email captured and a set follow-up time. A gate code goes only to a tenant.

questions.q: Karen moves in tomorrow at Escondido. What do you do today?
options: Nothing; she already has the date
Call to confirm her arrival time
Email her the whole rental agreement
Release the unit unless she has prepaid
questions.explanation: Confirm the arrival time the day before. It also catches plans that changed, like a closing moved to Monday.

questions.q: A new tenant asks, "Would you really sell my stuff?" What do you say?
options: "We'd never actually do that to anyone"
Explain the lien process calmly, as a fact
"Only if you really give us a reason to"
"You'd have to ask the manager about that"
questions.explanation: Explain the lien process the same way to everyone: a fact in the agreement, said kindly. Never soften it, never make it a threat.

questions.q: Which of these do you collect at every move-in?
options: A credit report and two references
An alternate contact and military status
A security deposit of one month's rent
A copy of a recent utility bill and a pay stub
questions.explanation: Photo ID, an alternate contact and military status are collected at every move-in. Greens charges no deposit.

questions.q: A Temecula boat owner says his own policy covers the boat in storage. What do you record in Cubby?
options: Nothing; take his word for it
The policy number and expiration
Greens' plan, added anyway to be safe
His insurance agent's home address
questions.explanation: Own policy: record the policy number and expiration date. Cubby raises a reminder task when proof is missing or expired.

questions.q: A web lead comes in at 9:50 PM, after hours. When do you call?
options: Right away, at 9:52 PM
First thing next business morning
Sometime in the next 48 hours
Only if they call the office first
questions.explanation: After-hours leads are the first call of the next business morning. Calls and texts stay inside 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

questions.q: A customer who rented online moved in yesterday. What do you still owe her?
options: Nothing, because she chose to rent online
A welcome call with the orientation
A paper copy of everything by mail
A visit to her unit to check her lock
questions.explanation: Online renters skip the counter orientation. A welcome call within a day covers the due date, late fee, autopay, protection and no living in units.

questions.q: A customer replies STOP to a text. You may send one more text to confirm the request.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A customer who replies STOP gets no more texts, right away. Note it in Cubby.

questions.q: A lead in Cubby shows the source Failed Checkout. What happened?
options: They rented online and paid in full
Their online payment did not go through
They sent a question through the contact form
They spoke with the voice agent after hours
questions.explanation: Failed Checkout means they tried to rent online and the payment failed. Call and offer to finish it with them.

questions.q: A Valley Center customer says the website showed a lower rate yesterday. What do you do?
options: Tell her the website must be out of date
Check Cubby and honor that price if it shows
Give her the lower rate, whatever Cubby says
Tell her to go rent online to get that rate
questions.explanation: Never argue. Check Cubby; if it shows that price for the unit, honor it. If you are unsure, ask your manager.

questions.q: A customer asks, "Why is there an admin fee?" Which answer fits?
options: "It's just how we make our money"
"It's a one-time setup charge"
"Everyone charges it, so don't worry"
"I can drop it for you this one time"
questions.explanation: Short and confident: one time, to set up the account. Quote it up front every time so nobody hears it first at the counter.

questions.q: A Murrieta caller says he needs to check with his wife. What do you offer?
options: A discount if he decides on this call
Email the quote, hold it, call when both home
To call him back sometime next month, if he wants
To hold the space for one hour only
questions.explanation: A shared decision needs both people. Email the quote, hold the space, and set a call for when they are both home.

questions.q: A tenant pays at the counter. What do you offer before she leaves?
options: A bigger unit at a better rate
Autopay
A free month for a review
A new disc lock from the office
questions.explanation: After every manual payment, offer autopay: she never has to think about it and is far less likely to see a late fee.

questions.q: A tenant gives notice because her house finally closed and she has room. What do you do?
options: Offer her a discount if she stays one more year
Thank her, confirm the steps, ask for a review
Warn her that rates may drop if she waits
Ask her to keep the unit one more month
questions.explanation: That is a happy ending. Do not push a save; confirm broom-clean and lock removed, and ask for a review and a referral.

questions.q: A tenant's unit was broken into. She asks whether she is covered. What do you say?
options: "Yes, the plan covers all theft"
Explain the claim path; they decide
"No, nothing is ever covered here"
"Greens will pay for what was taken"
questions.explanation: Explain the path, not the outcome: photos, a list, a police report number. The claims administrator or her insurer decides.

questions.q: An upset Escondido tenant's new rate is still below the street rate in Cubby. What may you say?
options: Nothing at all about the street rate
It is still below what a new customer pays
Her rate is now frozen for the next year
Rates should come back down again by next year
questions.explanation: Comparing to the street rate is fair when Cubby shows it is true. Never promise a frozen rate or a future drop.

questions.q: Rate-change notices go out next week. What should you do now?
options: Ask your manager for the reasons
Plan to say corporate decided it
Plan to guess the reasons if asked
Plan to say the system did it
questions.explanation: Ask your manager what is driving an increase before notices go out, so you answer with real reasons.

questions.q: When a long-time tenant is upset about a rate change, you may promise that the next increase will be smaller.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Never promise what you do not control: no reversal, no frozen rate, no smaller future increase. Offer options inside your authority.

questions.q: A tenant paid twice by mistake. Which tool sends the money back?
options: A waive
A refund
A credit
A write-off
questions.explanation: A refund sends money back to the card or account it came from. A waive cancels a charge; a credit waits for the next bill.

questions.q: Your manager approves waiving a late fee. What reason do you enter in Cubby?
options: "Customer asked"
"First late payment, goodwill"
"Waived per request of tenant today"
Leave it blank; the manager approved it
questions.explanation: Every waive carries a real reason. "Customer asked" is not a reason.

questions.q: A tenant asks why you can't take less. It is Greens' policy. What do you say?
options: "The system won't let me"
"Greens' policy is..."
"My computer locks me out of that"
"The law says I can't take less"
questions.explanation: Never blame the system for a policy; it is a misrepresentation. Say what is true.

questions.q: Which voicemail is right for a past-due tenant?
options: Your name, Greens and a number
"Hi, your rent is now past due"
"Your unit is close to going to lien"
"You owe [amount]; please call us back"
questions.explanation: Voicemail carries your name, Greens and a callback number, never the debt, balance or lien. Someone else may hear it.

questions.q: Which mean you stop collecting and call your manager the same day? Pick all that apply.
options: The tenant is on active military duty
A bankruptcy notice arrives
The tenant mentions a lawyer
The tenant asks for a payment link
questions.explanation: Military duty, bankruptcy, a death, a written dispute, a Declaration in Opposition or a lawyer: stop and escalate. A payment link is normal help.

questions.q: Greens follows FDCPA-style conduct rules on every collections contact, even though it is collecting its own rent.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The FDCPA mostly covers agencies, but California's Rosenthal Act and Texas Finance Code chapter 392 reach a business collecting its own debts. Greens follows the conduct rules everywhere.

questions.q: A tenant's autopay card was declined on the 1st. What kind of call is the first one?
options: A lien warning call
A service call
A final collection call
A move-out save call
questions.explanation: The failed autopay call is a service call: help the tenant update the card before a late fee posts.

questions.q: A tenant arrives shouting that his code failed after a two-hour drive. What do you do first?
options: Raise your voice so he can hear you
Lower your voice and let him finish
Tell him it was his own mistake
Call 911 the moment he raises his voice
questions.explanation: People match the volume around them. Calm, let him finish, play it back. Call 911 for threats or any safety concern.

questions.q: A caller who forgot her gate code wants it read over the phone. What do you do first?
options: Read it to her quickly
Verify who she is
Text it to whatever number she gives
Tell her to wait for the office to open
questions.explanation: A gate code is a password. Verify identity against the lease before you give or reset a code.

questions.q: A Fairfield tenant reports a cut lock and asks to see the camera footage. What do you say?
options: "Sure, come look at it with me now"
It is kept for the police
"We don't keep any camera footage"
"Only if you pay the footage fee"
questions.explanation: Preserve footage and gate logs; it goes to the police under Greens' rules, not to the tenant. Do not promise what it shows.

questions.q: A daughter tells you her father, a tenant, has died. What do you say first?
options: "Do you have the death certificate?"
"I'm so sorry for your loss."
"His rent is past due, unfortunately."
"I can open the unit for you right now."
questions.explanation: Condolence first, then the documents. No account details or access until your manager reviews them.

questions.q: If you suspect someone is living in a unit, you document what you saw and call your manager without approaching the unit.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Never approach alone, knock or open the door. Document dates, times and gate activity, and call your manager; where there is risk, the police.

questions.q: Someone at the counter asks whether her neighbor rents a unit at Greens. What do you say?
options: "Yes, he's in one of our 10x10s"
That you can't say who rents here
"Only if you are a family member"
"Let me look him up in Cubby for you"
questions.explanation: Everything about a tenant is private, even the fact that they rent from Greens.

questions.q: A coworker wants to offer $10 off to anyone who posts a review. What do you say?
options: "Fine, but only for five-star reviews"
"Greens offers no incentives"
"Fine, but only for long-time tenants"
"Fine, as long as it stays under $10"
questions.explanation: Greens offers no incentives for reviews of any kind, and buying positive reviews is banned.

questions.q: A one-star review says, "They auctioned my RV." What goes in the reply?
options: The dates each notice was sent
Sorry, no details, a number to call
The balance that was owed at the time
A note that every step was legal
questions.explanation: No account, lien or incident details in public. Template 4: empathy, no details, a number to call.

questions.q: A five-star review was posted this morning. When should it get a reply?
options: Within 48 hours
Within a month
Only negatives get replies
Whenever there is time
questions.explanation: Reply to every review within 48 hours, about 70 words, with your name and role.

questions.q: In practice, you score a coworker's call. How many things do you give her to work on?
options: Everything you noticed on the call
Two
None, only the score
At least five
questions.explanation: The score and two things to work on, never ten. Then read "what great looks like" together and swap.

questions.q: You play the customer in practice. If the staff member never asks what you are storing, you should tell them anyway.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The customer holds back what was not asked, just like a real caller.

questions.q: A family's 10-year-old offers to translate the lease terms. What do you do?
options: Let her translate, since she is willing
Bring in a Spanish-speaking teammate
Hand them the English copy to take home
Write out your own translation of the terms
questions.explanation: Never use a child for lease, lien or collections terms. Use a teammate or Greens' approved help, and check understanding.

questions.q: A Spanish-speaking customer asks for the contract in Spanish. What do you say?
options: "Sure, I'll translate it for you myself"
That you will ask your manager
"We never do that for anyone, sorry"
"Just use a translation app on your phone"
questions.explanation: Never promise a translated contract or negotiate mainly in Spanish without your manager. California Civil Code 1632 can apply.

questions.q: You glance at your job aid while a web reservation comes in at 2:10 PM. By when should you have called?
options: Tomorrow at 9:00 AM
questions.explanation: Web leads: first live contact within 5 minutes during open hours, 30 at the most.
